deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is section 18 of a draft continuation of Ramanujan's paper 'On certain trigonometrical sums and their applications in the theory of numbers' (Trans. Camb. Phil. Soc. 1918), as the archivist's note on the next page says. The stated aim is an expression for sum sigma_s(n) x^n and sum r_s(n) x^n that shows their behaviour for large s. Here sigma_s(n) is the sum of the s-th powers of the divisors of n, and r_s(n) is the number of representations of n as a sum of s squares. On this page only the sigma part is begun.

Step 1 (18.1). Take Re x > 0. The partial-fraction expansion of the hyperbolic cotangent gives
 pi*coth(pi x) = sum_{n in Z} 1/(x + n i),
with the sum taken symmetrically (n and -n paired). Expanding the left side as a geometric series in e^{-2 pi x} gives
 pi*coth(pi x) = pi*(1 + e^{-2 pi x})/(1 - e^{-2 pi x}) = pi + 2 pi * sum_{k>=1} e^{-2 pi k x}.
This is exactly (18.1).

Step 2 (18.11). Differentiate both sides s-1 times, s an integer >= 2. [Filled in by me:]
- The left side becomes 2 pi * sum_k (-2 pi k)^{s-1} e^{-2 pi k x}.
- The right side becomes (-1)^{s-1} (s-1)! * sum_n (x + n i)^{-s}.
- Cancelling (-1)^{s-1} and dividing by (2 pi)^s gives
 sum_{k>=1} k^{s-1} e^{-2 pi k x} = Gamma(s)/(2 pi)^s * sum_{n in Z} (x + n i)^{-s}.
This is the Lipschitz summation formula. For s >= 2 the right side converges absolutely, so no symmetric pairing is needed.

Ramanujan then states, without proof, that the theory of residues shows (18.11) holds for every real s > 1. This requires principal branches of (x + n i)^{-s}. It agrees with the general Lipschitz formula sum_n (tau + n)^{-s} = (-2 pi i)^s/Gamma(s) * sum_k k^{s-1} e^{2 pi i k tau}, taking tau = i x. In that substitution (i x + n)^{-s} = e^{-i pi s/2} (x - n i)^{-s}, and the phase cancels against (-2 pi i)^s.

Step 3. Replace x by n x in (18.11) and sum over n >= 1.
- On the left, sum_n sum_k k^{s-1} e^{-2 pi k n x} = sum_N sigma_{s-1}(N) e^{-2 pi N x}, by collecting the terms with k n = N.
- So sum_N sigma_{s-1}(N) e^{-2 pi N x} = Gamma(s)/(2 pi)^s * sum_{n>=1} sum_{m in Z} (n x + m i)^{-s}.

Step 4 (18.2). The double sum runs over half of the lattice Z x + Z i, namely n >= 1 with m in Z. It converges absolutely exactly when s > 2. [Filled in by me:] Write (n, m) = d(mu, nu) with d = gcd(n, m), so that (n x + m i)^{-s} = d^{-s} (mu x + nu i)^{-s} for d > 0 with principal branches. Summing over d produces the factor zeta(s). The pairs that remain are:
- (1, 0), which gives 1/x^s;
- coprime (mu, nu) with mu, nu >= 1, which give (mu x + nu i)^{-s} and (mu x - nu i)^{-s}.
Hence
 sum_N sigma_{s-1}(N) e^{-2 pi N x} = Gamma(s) zeta(s)/(2 pi)^s * {x^{-s} + sum_{(mu,nu)=1} (mu x + nu i)^{-s} + sum_{(mu,nu)=1} (mu x - nu i)^{-s}}.
This is (18.2), a non-integral-s form of the Eisenstein series written as a sum over primitive lattice points.

Intended application [my inference, not on the page]. For real x > 0 every |mu x +/- nu i| exceeds x, so for large s the bracket is dominated by x^{-s}. This would give sum sigma_{s-1}(n) e^{-2 pi n x} ~ Gamma(s) zeta(s)/(2 pi x)^s. The page breaks off before the r_s(n) case.
errors: No genuine mathematical errors were found.
(18.1) needs symmetric (principal-value) summation, since sum 1/(x + n i) is only conditionally convergent. Ramanujan's ordering 1/x + 1/(x+i) + 1/(x-i) + ... implicitly does this.
The extension of (18.11) to all real s > 1 is asserted without proof ('by the theory of residues'). It is true provided principal branches are used.
In (18.2) the condition gcd(mu, nu) = 1, with mu, nu >= 1, is left implicit. Without it the factor zeta(s) would be wrong.
Possible slip: the third term of (18.11) seems to be written 3^{-1} (or with the s barely visible) instead of 3^{s-1}.

results.what: pi + 2 pi * sum e^{-2 pi k x} = sum_{n in Z} 1/(x + n i), i.e. the partial-fraction expansion of pi coth(pi x)
results.modern_name: Mittag-Leffler / partial-fraction expansion of the cotangent

results.what: sum k^{s-1} e^{-2 pi k x} = Gamma(s)(2 pi)^{-s} sum_n (x + n i)^{-s}, for integer s and, via residues, for all real s > 1
sum sigma_{s-1}(n) e^{-2 pi n x} = Gamma(s) zeta(s)(2 pi)^{-s} times a sum of (mu x +/- nu i)^{-s} over coprime pairs, for real s > 2
results.modern_name: Eisenstein series as a lattice sum (Lambert series of sigma_{s-1}), extended to non-integral s, aimed at large-s asymptotics
results.usually_credited_to: Eisenstein/Hurwitz/Weierstrass for even integer s (19th century)

deep.surprise_reason: The ingredients are classical: the cotangent expansion, the Lipschitz formula and the lattice-sum form of Eisenstein series. The only mildly distinctive features are the use of non-integral s and the stated goal of large-s asymptotics for sigma_s and r_s generating functions. This fragment is an abandoned conclusion to his 1918 trigonometrical-sums paper and contains nothing beyond known results.

checkable.asserts: (18.1) at x = 0.7 with symmetric summation; the difference should be about 0, up to a truncation error of roughly 3e-5.
(18.11) for s = 3, x = 1; the difference should be about 0.
(18.11) for the non-integral value s = 5/2 with principal branch; the difference should be about 0.
(18.2) for s = 4, x = 1, summing over coprime mu, nu >= 1; the difference should be about 0 up to truncation.

transcription_corrections: In (18.11) the third term appears as '3^{-1}' (or '3^{s-1}' with a faint s) in the manuscript; 3^{s-1} is intended.
'a positive' is struck out and replaced by 'an integer greater than 1', which is correctly rendered.
